issue_context.title: [v20.6] CJS runs repeatedly when there are circular dependencies when loaded by ESM
issue_context.body:
### Version

v20.6.0

### Platform

all

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

https://github.com/liuxingbaoyu/node-v20.6-bug

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

always

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

```
node .\main.js
run
success
```

### What do you see instead?

```
node .\main.js
run
run
success
```

### Additional information

This should be the regression introduced by v20.6.
comments: Note that this is breaking`@babel/core`, and thus all the frameworks/project that use it. It would be great to prioritize it 🙏
Can someone give a reproducible example? The code from https://github.com/liuxingbaoyu/node-v20.6-bug doesn't show the problem (it throws an error in `mod/index.js`).

Sorry, I forgot to push the second commit.
But the initial error is also different due to the regression.
Please try again, thanks!
I have a repro. Starting to bisect.

@targos If it helps, it looks like the problem is that ESM's CJS loader doesn't set [this `loaded = true`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/5b31ff112783f97d12763a6516fcdadb7fa046ec/lib/internal/modules/cjs/loader.js#L909) before evaluating the CJS module.

Here probably: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/5b31ff112783f97d12763a6516fcdadb7fa046ec/lib/internal/modules/esm/translators.js#L326
Bug is introduced by https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47999

In case there is no easy fix, would it be possible to revert that PR?

(cc @aduh95)
Thanks for the ping, I'll have a look
To help with search, this is the issue for the error "TypeError: Cannot redefine property: File" generated in `@babel/core`. See https://github.com/babel/babel/issues/15927

Assuming angular tests would have  caught this, Should we add it to citgm? (The failure seem to break angular)

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/25782

> In case there is no easy fix, would it be possible to revert that PR?
> 
> (cc @aduh95)

The change from https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47999 is opt-in. Why not just stop opting in?
@rluvaton We are also working on https://github.com/nodejs/citgm/pull/628 (angular was broken through Babel)

> angular was broken through Babel

Same thing with astro: [withastro/astro #8411](https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/8411)

> @rluvaton We are also working on [nodejs/citgm#628](https://github.com/nodejs/citgm/pull/628) (angular was broken through Babel)

Jest (which is in CITGM already) also uses Babel, I'm surprised that wasn't discovered...
@SimenB This bug is only triggered when the ESM package uses a CJS package. :)

Jest's CI is failing now, I'd have thought those would have been caught.

EDIT: right, it's the build script (which is in ESM): https://github.com/jestjs/jest/actions/runs/6094016439/job/16535303696

CITGM result from v20.6.0 release: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/49185#issuecomment-1698005213. Apparently, `jest` broke but no one looked at these failures (that's why I suggested: https://github.com/nodejs/citgm/issues/955)

Stack: https://ci.nodejs.org/job/citgm-smoker/3212/nodes=fedora-last-latest-x64/testReport/junit/(root)/citgm/jest_v29_6_4/

Right, so there at least the error reported in this bug can be seen.

If Jest is known to be flaky on CITGM, I'd be happy to take a look. I don't think I've been pinged on any CITGM stuff since v19 release (https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/44626#issuecomment-1282191258)
When could we expect a release for the [fix](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/49500) that was merged ? 🙏

For people watching issue this for the error with Babel: we added a workaround in `@babel/core`, `@babel/traverse` and `@babel/types` 7.22.17. Please make sure to upgrade and they should be compatible with Node.js 20.6.0.

Anyone with a Quick fix, or which version is stable?
My version: `v20.6.0`
[v20.6.1](https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v20.6.1) is stable.

review_comments: What if a tool is modifying CommonJS modules after they’re loaded, by changing what’s in `require.cache`? I feel like that’s a valid use case, like in mocking or hot module reload; would this change break such behavior?
Should we add a test for this?
If it's testable, I think that's a good idea :)
Agree having a test sounds good, I don't plan on working on this without a repro though, so PR's welcome.
It looks like there is one: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/49497#issuecomment-1706232114
That's a repro of the core issue which there's already a test for. The question was specifically about the behaviour when modifying `require.cache`.

@aduh95 and @GeoffreyBooth,

This seems to be breaking Yarn's plug-n-play. I'll see if I can find a simple repo case.

At the moment, all I know is that it works in 20.5.1 and breaks in 20.6.1.

**Note:** Upgrading Yarn from 3.2.2 to 3.6.3 seems to fix the issue I'm seeing, but @GeoffreyBooth's point is valid:
> What if a tool is modifying CommonJS modules after they’re loaded, by changing what’s in `require.cache`? I feel like that’s a valid use case, like in mocking or hot module reload; would this change break such behavior?

I'm fairly confident that https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47999 is what is affecting PnP, but it didn't really broke it, did it? It only changed the CJS implementation to a one who is more limited, Yarn maintainers have been informed released a fix before it merged on Node.js side. Upgrading Yarn is the "correct" move forward. Anyway it's off topic, if you see an issue with an up-to-date version of Node.js and Yarn, please open a new issue.

@nicolo-ribaudo,

Yes, it worked in 20.6.0 and broke in 20.6.1.
